name: ARIES
question: Does once-daily mirabegron reduce incontinence episodes and micturition frequency versus placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults aged at least 18 years in the United States and Canada with at least three months of overactive bladder symptoms, at least eight micturitions and three grade 3/4 urgency episodes per 24 hours at baseline.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria and Study Procedures, p 1390

verdictNote: Both doses met both co-primary symptom endpoints versus placebo at 12 weeks.
takeaway: In ARIES, mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg once daily each reduced incontinence episodes and micturitions more than placebo over 12 weeks in adults with overactive bladder.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Auerbach S, Martin N, et al. "Results of a randomized phase III trial of mirabegron in patients with overactive bladder." *J Urol.* 2013;189(4):1388-1395. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.10.017

results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline to final visit (95% CI); FAS-I n=933: mirabegron 50 mg n=312, 100 mg n=296, placebo n=325

results.note: Within-arm change CIs; placebo-adjusted differences and their CIs are not reported.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: Two-week single-blind placebo run-in, then mirabegron 50 mg, mirabegron 100 mg, or placebo once daily for 12 weeks; visits at weeks 4, 8, and 12 and telephone follow-up 30 days later.
delivery.note: Overall study discontinuations: 13.3% with 50 mg, 12.2% with 100 mg, and 15.2% with placebo; adverse-event discontinuations: 4.1%, 4.4%, and 3.7%, respectively (Full text, Patient Disposition, p 1391).

relations.note: Companion phase 3 mirabegron trial in Europe, Australia, and South Africa with a tolterodine reference arm.
